body:
Several generators left expansion ground empty, scattered permanent deposits, or surrounded crops with rigid barriers. This change gives resources clearer locations and opens the requested terrain while preserving each map’s intended routes and opening supplies.

- Lava Shield: remove central void vents.
- The Comb: much denser inlet wheat/wood clumps and natural outer-edge patches.
- Honeycomb Isle: remove stone cell liners and restore hexagons as the default shape.
- Coral: add small sand-contained expansion courts (half-size courts with thin rings).
- Plantations: grant the selected starting workforce on every initially owned island, with per-settlement validation.
- Locust and Old Growth: jitter starting positions while preserving home room and separation.
- The Glacis: add wheat/wood along moat banks and inter-player rivers.
- Braided Delta: replace scattered resources with coherent fields, woods, small quarries, and mixed-fruit orchards.
- Shattered Coast: add separated resource clumps outside protected starting areas.
- Portage Lakes: remove wheat-field sand enclosures while retaining connecting trails and timber containment.

Generator revisions, focused contracts, Linux golden rows, and documentation are updated. Plantations opts into workers per starting swarm; other generators retain the existing per-colony worker policy. No simulation rules or saved-state formats change.

## Verification

Linux x86_64, GCC 15.2, fast development build (`-O0 -g1`) using the existing SDL3 dependency prefix. Focused builds, native contracts, generator sweeps, saved-map/game reloads, crop-growth checks, and paired 20,000-tick AI calibration games were run during implementation. Portage Lakes passed 74 generation cases, both focused/retained regressions, and all 12 refreshed Linux golden cases including 13–16 players.

The final combined regression run passed **9 cases and 6,658 assertions** on the committed source. Earlier focused checks cover Lava Shield, the Comb, and the separate Portage regressions. All **92 affected Linux golden rows** were refreshed (including 12 Portage cases).

[Review evidence and downloads](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/d2985581ba481332bf59e404fa67c22408a2dd68) include previews, requests/results, maps, saved games, native logs, source/binary SHA-256 manifests, and AI economy records. High-volume game logs are clearly labelled economy subsets with original-log hashes. Executable binaries are omitted.

[Final combined regression log](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/d2985581ba481332bf59e404fa67c22408a2dd68/final-contracts.log) · [Final source manifest](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/d2985581ba481332bf59e404fa67c22408a2dd68/final-source-manifest.json)

Coverage is native Linux only. These are generator output changes, not proof of cross-platform checksum equivalence, competitive balance, human playability, or release performance. Two crowded Old Growth requests retained their pre-existing refusal rather than being reported as passes. Single AI games have mixed economy outcomes and do not establish balance.
title: Refine map resources, terrain, and starting settlements
